note: `sim/mulligan.py`, written by `python tests/go_fixtures.py`. Floats are Float64bits: the verdict is a `<` against FLAT and the table is a sort, so one ulp is a different recommendation.

decks.name: naya
decks.why: three colours with duals, a five-colour land, wastes, a Sol Ring making two, a summoning-sick dork, two land fetchers, a Phyrexian cost that must demand nothing, a wholly generic cost, and a card past the horizon

decks.name: esper-rocks
decks.why: rocks rather than lands carry the colours; a rock makes three

decks.name: mono-green-poor
decks.why: 20 lands: an unmet requirement at every rung

decks.name: all-lands
decks.why: no nonland cards: the regression has no curve to fit

decks.name: no-lands
decks.why: no lands at all, and the whole 99 asking for colour

decks.name: uncastable
decks.why: 40 lands and 59 spells nobody can cast inside the horizon, so EVERY rule deploys exactly 0.0 and the ranking is decided entirely by the mulligan-rate tie-break -- which is the only way to see which direction it breaks in

decks.name: quarter-steps
decks.why: 34 lands and a handful of one-drops. Run at FOUR games, so every deployment figure is a whole number of spells over four and therefore an exact multiple of 0.25 -- which puts rows exactly `FLAT` apart, where `< FLAT` and `<= FLAT` choose different `gentlest` rules. The same trick as `tie-breaker` in the closed forms' decks, aimed at a different boundary

sweeps.label: naya
sweeps.why: a real three-colour deck with a commander, where colour screw and ramp both move the ranking

sweeps.label: esper-rocks
sweeps.why: rocks rather than lands, so the `min_mana_pieces` axis is the one that separates the rules

sweeps.label: mono-green-poor
sweeps.why: a deck the grid cannot rescue: most rules land within `FLAT` of the default, which is the `flat` verdict and the `gentlest` answer

sweeps.label: all-lands
sweeps.why: every hand keeps under every rule, so every row ties and `best` is decided purely by the grid's ORDER -- Python's `max` keeps the first, and a sort would keep the last

sweeps.label: no-lands
sweeps.why: no hand is ever keepable, so every rule mulligans to the floor and the whole grid ties at the bottom

sweeps.label: naya-off-grid
sweeps.why: an explicit rule list with the default NOT in it, which is the only way to reach the baseline fallback

sweeps.label: uncastable
sweeps.why: every rule deploys 0.0, so the whole ranking is the mulligan-rate tie-break and nothing else

sweeps.label: quarter-steps
sweeps.why: four games, so every deployment is an exact multiple of 0.25 and rows land exactly `FLAT` apart. The seed is 2 and it was SEARCHED for: at that seed a row exactly `FLAT` below the best mulligans half as often as anything inside the band, so `< FLAT` and `<= FLAT` name different `gentlest` rules -- which is the only way that boundary is visible from outside
